w: A working Ashkenazi synagogue on a quiet residential street a short walk from Lille's old town - modest from the outside, and easy to walk past unless you already know rue Auguste Angellie by name.
s: Lille's Ashkenazi synagogue, hiding in plain sight
_facts: Jewish congregation and synagogue at 5 rue Auguste Angellie, Lille
Congregation worships in the Ashkenazi rite

w: One of the largest Jesuit churches in all of France, tucked onto a street named for the military hospital that once stood nearby. It's been a monument historique since 1987, but still gets overshadowed by Lille's bigger-name basilicas and belfries.
s: One of France's largest Jesuit churches
_facts: Roman Catholic church on Rue de l'Hopital Militaire in Lille
Classified monument historique since 1987; one of the largest Jesuit churches in France, dedicated to Saint Stephen

w: Eleven hectares built in 1948 to inherit a botanical tradition going back to 1596, packed with an orangery of Mediterranean mimosa and oleander, a tropical greenhouse holding 12,000 plants - bananas, coffee, ginger, tree ferns - plus a dahlia collection and the city's own astronomical observatory.
s: Bananas and coffee plants growing under Lille's sky
_facts: 11-hectare municipal botanical garden established 1948, successor to city gardens dating from 1596
Orangery (1952) with Mediterranean plants; tropical greenhouse (1970) with about 12,000 plants; rose garden, dahlia collection and an astronomical observatory
